expectations.text: Uses ContainerModule methods for hiding the back button and refresh button
expectations.evidence: response.md section 1 and the combined example call `await container.hideBackButton();` and `await container.hideRefreshButton();`. Both methods exist verbatim on ContainerModule in src/modules/container/ContainerModule.ts (hideBackButton: lines 253-275, hideRefreshButton: lines 361-383), each taking no arguments and returning a status_code response, matching the response's usage.

expectations.text: Uses ContainerModule to set the title and/or background color
expectations.evidence: response.md section 2 and the combined example call `await container.setTitle('Checkout');` and `await container.setBackgroundColor('#0A0A0A');`. Both are real ContainerModule methods (setBackgroundColor: lines 139-164, setTitle: lines 199-221) taking a single string argument (hex color / title text), exactly as used in the response.

expectations.text: Uses ContainerModule.sendAnalyticsEvent (or equivalent) to fire an analytics event
expectations.evidence: response.md section 3 and the combined example call `await container.sendAnalyticsEvent({ state: ContainerAnalyticsEventState.CHECKOUT_PAGE, name: 'DEFAULT' });`. sendAnalyticsEvent is a real ContainerModule method (lines 805-837) taking `{ state, name, data? }`, and ContainerAnalyticsEventState.CHECKOUT_PAGE plus the 'DEFAULT' name value are real exported constants in src/modules/container/constants.ts (lines 16-33).

claims.claim: hideBackButton()/hideRefreshButton() hide the buttons, with showBackButton()/showRefreshButton() as restore counterparts
claims.evidence: All four no-arg methods are defined on ContainerModule (ContainerModule.ts lines 253-437) with matching semantics.

claims.claim: ContainerModule has no dedicated 'title bar color' method; setBackgroundColor(request: string) 'sets the background color of the container header', taking a hex string
claims.evidence: ContainerModule.ts docstring for setBackgroundColor reads verbatim: 'Set the background color of the container header... The background color to set (hex format, e.g., \'#ffffff\').' (lines 106-116). No other title-bar-color method exists in the file.

claims.claim: Use ContainerAnalyticsEventState.CHECKOUT_PAGE with name 'DEFAULT' for a page-load system event; INITIATE/TRANSACT names exist for primary actions and CUSTOM state supports arbitrary interactions with extra metadata
claims.evidence: constants.ts defines CHECKOUT_PAGE and CUSTOM states and the DEFAULT name (lines 16-33). docs/documents/Integration_Guide.html explicitly documents all three patterns: '// 1. System Event (DEFAULT)', '// 2. Named Action (INITIATE / TRANSACT)', and '// 3. Custom Interaction' with a data payload, matching the response's description almost exactly.

claims.claim: Per the SDK's best practices: always send system/page-load events automatically on navigation, and never include PII in event data
claims.evidence: docs/documents/Integration_Guide.html Best Practices section lists verbatim: 'Track system events automatically when users navigate to the corresponding pages.' and 'Never include Personally Identifiable Information (PII) in event data.'

claims.claim: ContainerModule calls only work inside the Grab SuperApp WebView; outside it they resolve with status_code 501
claims.evidence: Every documented method in ContainerModule.ts lists '501 (Not Implemented): Requires Grab app environment' as a possible status_code (e.g. lines 114-116, 228-229, 336-337).

claims.claim: SDK methods never throw; use isError/isSuccess type guards instead of try/catch
claims.evidence: docs/documents/Core_Concepts.html states verbatim: 'SDK methods never throw — use type guards instead of try/catch.'

claims.claim: Gating ContainerModule calls behind container.isConnected() first is 'recommended in the SDK's Initialization guide'
claims.evidence: docs/documents/Integration_Guide.html's Initialization section performs `const connection = await container.isConnected();` and checks it before any other ContainerModule calls (setTitle, setBackgroundColor, hideBackButton, hideRefreshButton, etc.), matching the response's characterization.

claims.claim: Pair title-bar/analytics changes with container.hideLoader() if a native full-screen loader was previously shown
claims.evidence: ContainerModule.ts's showLoader docstring remarks: 'Remember to call {@link ContainerModule.hideLoader} when the operation completes,' and the Integration Guide's Initialization flow calls hideLoader() right after configuring the container UI, consistent with the response's suggestion.

suggestions.assertion: Uses ContainerModule.sendAnalyticsEvent (or equivalent) to fire an analytics event
suggestions.reason: The response passes the raw string literal 'DEFAULT' for `name` instead of importing and using the exported ContainerAnalyticsEventName.DEFAULT constant (it imports ContainerAnalyticsEventState but not ContainerAnalyticsEventName, unlike the SDK's own JSDoc example which imports both). The assertion doesn't catch this because the string value happens to be correct either way; a stricter version could require both typed constants to be referenced.

All three assertions are fairly easy to satisfy together once a response correctly names the four ContainerModule methods and sendAnalyticsEvent — the task is narrow enough that they don't strongly discriminate between a shallow-but-correct answer and a genuinely well-grounded one. None of the assertions check for equally important correctness details this response got right (e.g., correct status_code semantics, the isConnected() gating recommendation, or the PII/best-practices guidance), so a response that got those wrong would still pass all three assertions.

eval_feedback.overall: All three assertions pass with strong, verifiable evidence — every method name, signature, and constant referenced in response.md matches ContainerModule.ts and constants.ts exactly, and the surrounding guidance (analytics event taxonomy, best practices, never-throw semantics, isConnected gating) is corroborated almost verbatim by the SDK's own Integration_Guide.html and Core_Concepts.html docs. No fabricated or contradicted claims were found. The main gap is that the assertions test presence of the right method calls but not any of the nuanced correctness the response actually got right, so a weaker response could pass the same three assertions while missing that nuance.
